A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RARE/CRRF and RedQA research. All 26 pages in each version, including figures, tables, equations and Appendices A–F, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original retrieval experiments, 480-item human validation, end-to-end RAG results and repeated-run CRRF ablations (Sections 4–5 and Appendices D–E).

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results, including retrieval Tables 3 and 9–12, end-to-end RAG Table 4 and CRRF Tables 13–15.

M1.justification: The atomic-information selection, redundancy tracking, question generation and CRRF procedures are unchanged. Figure 2 replaces two 'SepRRF' labels with 'CRRF', matching the existing method description without changing the procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same Finance, Patent, Legal and General-Wiki corpora, 1–4-hop tasks, HotpotQA ablation data and benchmark-overlap comparisons. No coverage is added or removed.

E2.justification: The same nine retrievers appear in Table 3 and Appendix D. The Vanilla, Combined and Separate prompting comparisons with Base, MinMax and RRF aggregation also retain identical membership in Tables 13–14.

E3.justification: Retrieval metrics, top-10 evaluation, sample counts and model configurations are unchanged. Both retain the 480-item human evaluation, 100-passage HotpotQA ablation and GPT-5 Mini generation with GPT-5 judging for end-to-end evaluation.

E4.justification: The CRRF ablations, stability analysis, hop-depth comparisons, end-to-end coverage decomposition and qualitative examples are retained unchanged. Appendix table movements introduce no new analyses.

E5.justification: Both disclose sampling seed 42 in Appendix A.2 and five runs per CRRF configuration in Appendix E. Mean reporting and the coefficient-of-variation analysis in Table 15 are unchanged.

E6.justification: Matched numerical and qualitative results are unchanged throughout. For example, Qwen3-8B's 4-hop PerfRecall@10 remains 66.4% on General-Wiki, 8.5% on Finance, 27.9% on Patent and 5.0% on Legal (Figure 5 and Tables 9–12).

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and reasoning in Section 3, including candidate sets and reciprocal-rank aggregation, are unchanged. Appendix A.3 retains the same similarity and redundancy definitions; no proofs or formal assumptions are added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions and conclusion retain the same claims about RARE, CRRF, RedQA and retrieval weaknesses in high-overlap corpora.

C2.justification: Interpretations of similarity, redundancy, hop-depth degradation and generator behavior are unchanged. The Limitations section retains the same qualifications concerning LLM biases, the fixed similarity threshold, CRRF generalization, question naturalness and uncontrolled training differences.

D1.justification: Appendix A.2 implementation details, Appendix A.6 construction costs and Appendix F prompt descriptions are unchanged. No code or data access instructions are added or revised.

R1.justification: Section 2 and the cited research are unchanged. The bibliography shifts with pagination, but no research references or substantive positioning statements are added or removed.

P1.justification: v2 adds a funding Acknowledgments section before References and corrects Figure 2 terminology from 'SepRRF' to 'CRRF'. The existing scientific prose and section organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 2 updates its two ranking-stage labels. The acknowledgment addition reflows the references and appendices, shifting several tables relative to the text; figure content and table structures otherwise remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v2 resolves Figure 2's inconsistent 'SepRRF' labels by matching the established 'CRRF' terminology and adds previously absent funding disclosure. These modestly improve clarity and transparency, while the scientific content and evidential strength remain unchanged.
